items.title: David Weinstein Interview, 1988-09-22
items.q: He wouldn't use Bill Bourgeois. Isn't that funny?

ctx.x: No, no, no. Schalke had his own band up there. As a matter of fact, Barry Pollock recorded a couple of those things with him and he had some fine guys. I don't think he had too many local guys. I think Frankie Federico might have made a couple with him, of course Frankie was up there then with Louie, but he had really all guys from let's say the New York

area. He wouldn't use Bill Bourgeois. Isn't that funny? I don't know why. Yeah. But you know, it always struck me as strange. I think Bill was a little hurt, you know. He's working with Schalke and Schalke with the New Zealand on the record, maybe. I don't know. Bill played a pretty good player in the two. Well, you recorded with Schalke too, didn't you?

Well, that was done down here. We made a record down here. And one side of that was Yes She Does, No She Don't, and I forget the Everybody Lows My Baby or something like that was on the other side. Yeah, I remember that. We made that in the Roosevelt Hotel. And strangely enough, the guy who founded Decca was the guy who recorded that thing. It was the name Cap. Dave or Jack, one of the two. Yeah, he was in, he was the one that made the session. I remember that.
